questions.prompt: Which is the right way to store passwords?
questions.explanation: Passwords need a slow, salted one-way hash. Encryption is reversible; SHA-256 is too fast.

questions.prompt: Login should return different error messages for 'no such user' and 'wrong password' so users know what to fix.
questions.explanation: Distinct messages enable user enumeration. Return one generic 401.

questions.prompt: A logged-in customer calls POST /services (owner only). Correct response?
Customer A requests GET /bookings/18 which belongs to customer B and receives it. What is the bug?
questions.explanation: The server authenticated A but did not verify A owns booking 18.

questions.prompt: Which cookie flags help protect a session cookie?
questions.explanation: HttpOnly blocks JS access, Secure forces HTTPS, SameSite limits cross-site sending. Long expiry increases risk.

questions.prompt: What does the OAuth state parameter prevent?
questions.explanation: State binds the callback to the browser that started the flow.

questions.prompt: A Google login arrives with the same email as an existing password account. Safest behaviour?
options: Require email_verified AND confirmation of the existing password before linking
questions.explanation: Verified email plus password confirmation prevents account takeover through pre-hijacking.

questions.prompt: Which header check helps defend cookie-authenticated POST routes from CSRF?
questions.explanation: Reject state-changing requests whose Origin is not on your allowlist.

questions.prompt: CORS prevents a server from receiving malicious requests.
questions.explanation: CORS only restricts which origins' scripts can read responses in the browser.

questions.prompt: A secret was committed and then deleted in the next commit. What must you do?
options: Rotate the secret (and optionally purge history)
questions.explanation: Git history still contains it. Treat it as compromised and rotate.

questions.prompt: Why run integration tests against a real Postgres in CI?
options: They catch constraint, SQL and transaction behaviour that mocks hide
It is faster than unit tests
questions.explanation: Constraints, queries and locking only behave truly against the real database.

questions.prompt: POST /signup body contains {"role":"owner"}. What should happen?
options: Field is ignored; role is customer
questions.explanation: Only allow-listed fields are read; privileged fields are set by the server.
